newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kazakhstan says to buy $114 mln Deere harvesters.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan says to buy $114 mln Deere harvesters.

text.p: A spokesman for the ExImbank of Kazakhstan said on Wednesday the bank had signed a contract with Deere and Co of the United States to buy $114 million in John Deere grain and cotton harvesters for 1997 delivery.
"The contract was signed on Monday between U.S. John Deere and the ExImbank of Kazakhstan," Isakhan Akylbekov told Reuters.
He said that the ExImbank of the United States would finance 85 percent of the $114 million deal and foreign commercial banks would finance the remaining 15 percent.
The Central Asian republic would take delivery of 630 grain combines and 100 cotton combines next year for use in the 1997 harvest.
"John Deere will invest $3 million in a joint venture for servicing its combines," Akylbekov added.
An official Turkmenistan newpaper said Deere had made a separate $74 million sale of agricultural equipment to Turkmenistan.
The Dashkhovuzskaya Pravda newpaper said the deal would be over five years and be financed by the U.S. ExImbank but gave no further details.
It said the U.S. bank had financed a $54 million agricultural equipment deal for the Central Asian republic in 1994.
